title: Meta: link to web-platform-tests (in header?)
body:
Other WHATWG standards link to their web-platform-tests directories prominently in their headers, see https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/ or https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/ for examples.

We should link to at least these directories and labels:
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/2dcontext
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/custom-elements
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/eventsource
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/html
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/imagebitmap-renderingcontext
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/innerText
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/offscreen-canvas
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/shadow-dom
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/webmessaging
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/websockets
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/webstorage
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/workers

Not sure about:
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/conformance-checkers ( @sideshowbarker?)
- https://github.com/w3c/web-platform-tests/tree/master/html-imports (@domenic?)

That's a lot of directories, too many to link to in the header?

The "use case" is two-fold:
- Advertising that web care about the test suites.
- If (almost) all specs link to their test suites, one can begin to write tooling that makes sure that every spec out there has a test suite, and that everything in wpt corresponds to some spec. (But yes, such a mapping could be maintained elsewhere.)

Related: https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/3010
Slightly related: https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/354
